title: Circles Builds: Shinya’s 2014 Sycip 26″ Hardtail – John Watson
content:
Over the next few weeks, we’ll be sharing builds from the Nagoya-based Circles bike shop. Starting it off with a very special Sycip 26″ hardtail Jeremy Sycip built for Tanaka-san back in 2010…

It all began with a fork. “I got the fork, new old stock, from a swap meet,” began Tanaka-san, as we chatted about his prized possession: a beautiful Sycip 26″ hardtail. “So then I asked Jeremy, ‘Can you build me a bike for this fork?’ and this is the result.” In the 1990s, moto manufacturer RS Taichi collaborated with Showa, a cycling brand, and produced a number of suspension forks in Japan.

On display here is the embodiment of the Circles approach to bike builds. Take a piece of Japan – in this case, the fork – and the Shimano components, and mix them into the zeitgeist of the global maker community.

Framebuilder Jeremy Sycip took the axle-to-crown dimensions of the RS Taichi Showa fork and began to design a bike geometry best suited to fit 26″ wheels and rim brakes. Recalling the order, Jeremy told me, “I found an old invoice, and it says retro MTB for Shinya.” The Santa Rosa, California-based builder used a blend of his favorite tubing, as well as his signature Sycip dropouts, Mountain Goat headtube rings, and his signature wishbone seat stays, complete with a 2¢ refund: two pennies are silver-soldered to the seat stay tops.

The standout detail on this vintage-inspired bike is the white rack, which is designed to support a small bag and bolts directly to the seat stay and cantilever bosses. Paul brakes provide the stopping power, along with Paul levers and Shimano XT components. A Nitto post, WTB saddle and grips manage the contact points. For tires, the Panaracer Smoke and Dart provide the traction, and gold Velocity Aeroheat rims laced to Chris King hubs add the bling factor. The cockpit includes 2014 SimWorks components.

A turquoise Chris King headset is the cherry on top of what has to be one of the sexiest vintage hardtails in memory…

Interested in a custom creation of your own? Check out Sycip Designs. Live in Japan and would like a curated build? Holler at Circles.
